fixed_constraints: I45 imposes complete macos-15 candidate gates operating PostgreSQL 17, Node 24 with pinned Playwright Chromium, the pinned Bun archive, and TypeScript 7.0.2, while release uploads, credentialed signing, and live provider calls stay forbidden.
The suite runs whole: go tests in all packages, 850 bun runtime tests, cataloguegen, modcheck, gramcheck, gofmt, vet, and strict tsc across fresh emit; a fully serviced local run shows zero skips.
I44 removed tscheck/ and tsc.yml together with their committed goldens, forcing TypeScript gating to be rebuilt on fresh emit instead of adapted from includes.
Each required service gets a setup script or command, each pin gets a committed lockfile or target record, and each real no-run row gets a written justification.
common.purpose: Resolve three I45 gate design points for the Can tree: the CI topology, the fresh-emit-to-TypeScript mechanism, and the TS gate evidence level.

emit_evidence.background: Fresh-emit TypeScript gating in CI may live in the job log alone or also persist the emit tree and tsc log as downloadable artifacts.
facts: Verifier and release-qualify already store test logs, qualification reports, and integrity records as artifacts, making upload an established idiom.
Persisted emit lets future readers audit precisely what tsc accepted, whereas log-only output fades with run-log retention.
Uploads spend storage and minutes per push and pull request; log streaming spends only the runner time already paid.

gate_topology.background: Candidate gating spans the Go suite, bun suite, live SQL/browser legs, mirrors, and fresh-emit tsc on macos-15, inside either one grown job or several operated gates.
facts: Today verifier executes a go test subset operating just the Bun archive, leaving database, browser, and strict-TS legs to skip quietly in CI.
Without docker on macos-15, PostgreSQL comes from brew services, Chromium from npm with a pinned Playwright install, and tsc from a committed lockfile.
A single job shares one setup and reports one verdict; split gates localize failures per family while duplicating setup and workflow files.

tscheck_mechanism.background: Strict tsc needs fresh TypeScript from every maintained example, produced by a reviewable step that also runs locally.
facts: The staged stdlib test already asserts plus builds all eight projects with identical rebuilds, so a dist copy under an env flag reuses the proven path in roughly ten lines.
A separate Go emitter would restage bundles and builds beside the suite, creating a parallel emitter free to drift from tested behavior.
Either path executes ahead of tsc in one job against one bundle archive, converging whenever the common build logic agrees.
